records.title: Armed two-step delete
records.summary: Deleting an entity listed in the UI is a two-step, in-place action with auto-disarm; no confirm() dialogs for these.

do: carry .arm-del with data-arm-label and a matching aria-label
arm on first activation (label becomes 'Confirm delete'), delete on second
auto-disarm after 4s, on Escape, outside click, or menu close
announce the result afterwards (banner or toast)
dont: no arming as a substitute for feedback

records.title: High-stakes confirmations
records.summary: Irreversible, security-relevant, or multi-item actions keep a native confirm() whose sentence names the object and consequence.

do: name the object and the consequence in the sentence
reason-bearing reject/decline decisions pair the confirm with a required, labelled reason field recorded in history
dont: do not route entity deletes through confirm() (use arming)
body.quote: Representative set: remove account · reset tokens · rebuild the index · clear a chat · enable auto-apply · approve a risky plugin.

records.title: Colour is never the only signal
records.summary: Status and meaning are carried by text or icon as well as colour; charts must survive greyscale and colour-blindness.

do: vary dash patterns or annotate in charts
dont: no colour-only dots or fills for meaning
body.quote: Do not rely on colour alone: label lines directly, vary dash patterns, or annotate.

records.title: Page hierarchy
records.summary: One element, one token and one job per level: page title → section heading → card heading → body → meta. Don't skip levels.

do: let a long page title wrap at --fs-page-title
dont: don't shrink a page title with inline font-size
don't use a section heading as a card label
body.quote: Don't skip levels or spend a level you don't need.

records.title: Copy helper owns the clipboard
records.summary: Use the shared cp() helper / .copy element; the helper owns fallback and confirmation labelling.

dont: never call navigator.clipboard from page code
body.quote: The helper owns the fallback and the confirmation labelling.

records.title: Native confirm() for one-way actions
records.summary: Actions that are irreversible, security-relevant, or affect more than the clicked item keep a native confirm() whose sentence names the object and the consequence (INTERACTION.md, one-way set). Arming cannot carry the consequence; this is the sanctioned stop, and never a substitute for the armed pattern on ordinary entity deletes.

body.when: irreversible, security-relevant, or wider than the clicked item: remove account, reset tokens, rebuild the index, clear a chat, enable an auto-apply mode, approve a plugin with a browser view
body.form: onsubmit="return confirm('...')" on the form; kept apostrophe-safe
body.copy: name the object and the consequence in the sentence; route entity deletes through arming instead
body.never: routine entity deletes (use the armed pattern), async flows, or as a shortcut to avoid designing the armed control
